inlines.value: Applying the transformation at a sink
Retaining complete documents alongside selected columns
single message transformation (SMT) converts the JSON strings in MongoDB change event
values. It retains the change event envelope, record key, headers, source metadata, and operation. The resulting events can be processed by transformations such as

You can configure a fixed projection to select document paths, assign output names, and convert values to specified Connect types. Without a matching projection, the SMT infers a schema from the document images in each event, using the existing MongoDB BSON converter. An inferred schema can vary between events and can contain nested structs or arrays. For production pipelines that require stable relational columns, configure a fixed projection for each collection that the sink consumes. The configured names and types define the output schema even when source fields disappear or change shape. Changing the projection configuration can change that schema and requires coordination with the sink’s table schema and any schema compatibility rules.

Apply this SMT to the JDBC sink connector to retain the original MongoDB change events in Kafka. A separate MongoDB sink can consume the same topic using a handler that understands Debezium MongoDB events. That sink must support the original MongoDB event format; converting events for a JDBC sink does not add MongoDB source support to other sink implementations.

Configure the sink’s key and value converters to deserialize the Kafka records with their Connect schemas. For example, use schema-enabled JSON or an appropriate schema-aware converter. The SMT expects a schemaful Debezium envelope.

The mapping configuration describes Kafka Connect types and does not require an Avro schema, Avro serialization, or a schema registry. The connector’s converters determine the Kafka wire format. The source and sink converters must agree on the format of the records already in the topic. Enabling schemas on the sink alone cannot recover Connect schemas from schema-less JSON records.

For date types, numeric values are epoch days, and strings use ISO local dates. For unzoned time types, numeric values use the declared output unit, and strings use ISO local times. Conversions reject overflow or fractional precision that the output type cannot represent. A BSON timestamp’s increment orders operations within a second and is not a fractional time; conversion to a temporal value uses only its unsigned seconds component. Use
to retain both components. Precise decimal types reject non-finite numbers; use a string or JSON representation if those values must be retained.

The schema is inferred independently for each event, without retaining fields from previous events. When a field is absent from both images of a later event, it is absent from that event’s inferred schema. Conflicting structures, such as a document changing to a scalar, produce an error identifying the document path. Inference also retains the existing BSON converter’s type and array limitations. Missing fields in an inferred schema have null values in the corresponding document image. Configured projections always keep their optional fields and return null for unresolved paths.
